name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 85

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Think how to give an image back

blocks.note: second meaning: what a mirror does with light

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a mirror produces an image.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both careful pondering and a mirror throwing light or a picture back towards the viewer.

clue.text: Gets round to some nonsense over a set-up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from the bottom letter to the top

explanation.surface: Someone finally dealing with some nonsense about an arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets round to' looks like a phrase, but 'Gets round' is the definition and 'over' places ROT above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns about an axis, like a wheel, spins or revolves in a circle.

clue.text: Book a blonde servant from Scotland

blocks.note: of a Scottish city on the Tay

explanation.surface: A golden-haired domestic who hails from north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Walter Scott novel, and the wordplay describes its title literally: Perth is a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fair Maid of Perth is an 1828 historical novel by Sir Walter Scott.

clue.text: Animal of a novel kind

indicators.note: made of means the letters come out of the words that follow

blocks.note: end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A creature of a new and unusual type.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is a large deer, called the moose in North America, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Fool making an escape from port

indicators.note: something that escapes from a place is no longer in it

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters leave

explanation.surface: An idiot slipping out of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is Antwerp in Belgium; lose its opening AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, annoying person, an informal British word for an idiot.

clue.text: All out to make a hit

blocks.note: first meaning: workers all out are on a stoppage

explanation.surface: A batter going all out to connect with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All out' sounds like maximum effort, but it is the union call for every worker to down tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a workers' stoppage, when everyone walks off the job, and also the act of landing a blow.

clue.text: Old money reigns supreme

blocks.note: first meaning: a former British gold coin worth a pound

explanation.surface: Inherited wealth still dominates society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old money' suggests aristocratic wealth, but it is an old British gold coin worth one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a former British pound coin and, as an adjective, a ruler or state holding supreme authority.

clue.text: Dance with the odd graduate

blocks.note: rum means odd or strange in old British slang

explanation.surface: Taking the floor with a strange university leaver.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in four-four time, one example of a dance.

clue.text: Flabbergasted at being struck out of line

blocks.note: second meaning: literally hit off course to one side

explanation.surface: Someone astonished to be punched out of a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stunned or overwhelmed, and read literally it describes being hit so you veer off to one side.

clue.text: Cretan made squiffy by drink

indicators.note: squiffy means tipsy, and a tipsy word staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Crete gets tipsy on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, and the word is used for any delicious beverage.

clue.text: One of the two brings three back for star performance

indicators.note: going back means the referenced answer is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: one of a pair born together

explanation.surface: A twin pulls off a trio of tricks for a starring turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three' is not a number but a cross-reference: it stands for the answer at 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkle is the glint or sparkle a star gives off, so it is literally what a star performs.

clue.text: Leave low in vessel

indicators.note: being in a vessel means sitting inside its walls, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
to low is to make a cow's sound

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave something low down inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not a height but the noise cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is American slang for clearing off or departing in a hurry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: If he comes again he'll be one for a beating

definitions.text: If he comes again he'll be one for a beating

blocks.clueFragment: If he comes again he'll be one for a beating
blocks.note: surface reading: a man who returns will be thrashed
setter's reading: say the name twice and you get a drum that is struck

explanation.surface: A warning that a man who shows up again will get a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubled, the name makes TOM-TOM, a hand-beaten drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom is a man's name, and repeating it gives tom-tom, a drum played by striking it.

clue.text: Where to buy collection that includes high-class hair-do vessel

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them within its own boundaries

blocks.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Shopping for a posh hairstyle kit and a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: U is crossword shorthand for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A large self-service store is the everyday place where people go shopping for groceries and household goods.

clue.text: The lady puts a sailor up in the old queen's place

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting something up means reading it from the bottom

explanation.surface: A woman hoisting a seaman in the realm of a former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Sheba is the biblical queen who visited Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom ruled by the queen who visited King Solomon in the Bible.

clue.text: Firmness of character needed to give book back

blocks.note: second meaning: the bound edge of a volume

explanation.surface: It takes resolve to return a borrowed book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give book back' reads like returning a library loan, but 'book back' is the part of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with courage is said to have backbone, and a volume's bound edge carrying the title is also called this.

clue.text: To be a flirt I'd plan her ruin

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A would-be seducer plotting how to bring a woman down.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, so the verb matches flirting exactly.

clue.text: Not a naval vessel one could plunder

blocks.note: first meaning: a privately owned armed ship, not part of the navy
second meaning: a person licensed to raid enemy shipping

explanation.surface: A ship outside the navy that a pirate could raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ship was privately owned yet licensed by a government to attack and rob enemy merchant shipping.

clue.text: One gas of a number no longer here, it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

blocks.note: several people who have left are gone

explanation.surface: A gas belonging to a group of people who have departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas making up about one percent of the air.

clue.text: Expert staff taking one in for testing time

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

explanation.surface: Skilled employees bringing someone in to try them out.
explanation.definitionFit: A probation is a trial period during which a new employee or offender is watched and assessed.

clue.text: What must be paid to hold name of royalty

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within one's grasp

explanation.surface: The fee for keeping a royal title.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a male member of a royal family, so he is one of royalty.

clue.text: Medal one held on the way out

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside something else

blocks.note: gong is slang for a medal

explanation.surface: A retiring officer clutching a decoration as they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone going is in the act of leaving or departing, so they are on the way out.

clue.text: Vessel gone astray with everyone aboard

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters scatter
those aboard are carried inside a vehicle

explanation.surface: A ship lost at sea with all hands on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship with several decks, used by Spain for war and trade.

clue.text: Meaning to show presumption

blocks.note: first meaning: what is suggested by words
second meaning: an inference drawn without being stated

explanation.surface: Someone intending to display arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaning to' looks like 'intending to', and presumption looks like arrogance; both are senses of something implied.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers the unstated sense carried by a remark and the conclusion one is entitled to draw from it.

clue.text: One finds poor Eric in the cooler

indicators.note: poor means in a bad state, so the name is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone discovers unlucky Eric locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like slang for prison but is the comparative of cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning colder or more frosty.

clue.text: What's stored may turn up in battered tin

indicators.note: turning a word upside down in a down answer flips its order
something battered is knocked out of shape
in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: Supplies kept in a dented can might come to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is data entered and held in a computer, the material fed into storage.

clue.text: Some of the fellows held at some length

indicators.note: taking only some of the following word means a run of letters sits inside it
the letters are held within the word just named

blocks.note: the run of letters after the opening f

explanation.surface: Some men being detained for quite a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth, about forty-five inches, so it is a unit of length.

clue.text: Sort of writing you'd swear by?

definitions.text: Sort of writing you'd swear by?

blocks.clueFragment: Sort of writing you'd swear by
blocks.note: surface reading: a text you trust completely
setter's reading: writing given to cursing, read as a pun on the word for oaths

explanation.surface: A style of script so reliable you'd vouch for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as CURSE plus -IVE, as if it meant inclined to swearing; it really means joined-up handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursive is joined-up flowing handwriting, the kind taught in schools as running script.

clue.text: Spend a long time getting across

blocks.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: Taking ages to make it over to the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey across water, or the act of crossing from one side to another.

clue.text: She'll take one to court

blocks.note: second meaning: bring a lawsuit against someone

explanation.surface: A woman intends to start legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is not a pronoun here but stands for a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a common female first name, and the verb means to bring legal proceedings against someone.

clue.text: Keep quiet at the rear perhaps and one won't keep everything

indicators.note: perhaps marks the word as just one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone hushing at the back who won't hog everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who divides things with others gives away part of what they have rather than retaining all of it.

clue.text: Most conclusive argument for disloyalty

indicators.note: conclusive here means forming the conclusion, so only the closing letter counts

blocks.note: a reason is an argument for something

explanation.surface: The clinching case for a charge of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most conclusive' reads as a superlative but means the last letter of Most.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or sovereign, the gravest form of faithlessness.
